purpose: What each source's own terms say about quoting it, read once and written down so that neither a permission nor a refusal has to be worked out twice. The site promises in six languages that an organisation may ask not to appear; this is where that promise is kept, and where a reading of a published notice is recorded with the sentence it rests on.

sources.quote: no se permite la reproducción y/o publicación, total o parcial, del sitio web, ni su tratamiento informático, su distribución, su difusión, ni su modificación, transformación o descompilación, ni demás derechos reconocidos legalmente a su titular, sin el permiso previo y por escrito del mismo
sources.finding: The notice reserves reproduction and publication of the site, in whole or in part, to prior written permission, and limits the material to personal and private use. Every record here rests on words quoted from its source, so a record that cannot carry its quotes cannot meet the evidence rule. Linking was never in question: the same notice contemplates third-party hyperlinks that open the full page and say nothing misleading.
sources.route: Permission is reserved rather than refused. Asking in writing would settle it, and the operator publishes its address in the same notice.

sources.quote: La reproduction des contenus est autorisée à titre pédagogique sous réserve des conditions suivantes : [...] Citation explicite de la (ou les) source(s) du document, y compris les images. [...] Gratuité de la diffusion.
sources.finding: The notice forbids reproduction in general and then authorises it for educational use under three conditions: the content is not altered, the source is cited explicitly, and distribution is free. This project meets all three — it quotes without altering, cites the address and the day it was read, and charges nobody. Recorded so that a later pass does not read this notice again, and does not mistake the opening sentence for the whole of it.
